steps.message:
Done, but with one deviation you should know about: `client.py` is shared by `scripts/sync_staging.py` **and** `scripts/export_prod.py` (the nightly finance export against `https://reports.example.com`). A hardcoded `verify=False` would have silently disabled certificate validation for production traffic too, which is not what the self-signed staging cert justifies.

So instead of hardcoding it, verification is now opt-out per environment:

- `client.py` — both `requests.get` calls pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` and defaulting to on.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` alongside the existing base-URL default, so staging runs unverified as you wanted.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; keeps verifying.

Note `urllib3` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on staging runs. I left it in place as a visible signal rather than suppressing it; say the word if you want it silenced.

Checks run: syntax parse of all three files only. No test suite in the repo and no network access to the staging host, so the request path itself is unverified.

If you genuinely want verification off everywhere including prod, tell me and I'll make it unconditional.
